summary: p95 spike from PCIe bus saturation during noisy training job on dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (HorizonsAI, dedicated pool) reports intermittent P95 spikes and streaming request timeouts between 2026-03-12 22:30 and ongoing. Trend shows sustained throughput drop for a subset of nodes in their reserved pool coincident with a large background training job scheduled by an internal research tenant.

Impact:
- Customer experiencing elevated p95 and ~2% of streaming sessions timeout with 504.
- Throughput for rw-open-7b-v2 endpoints on customer pool dropped ~40% for an hour and recovered with manual remediation.
- Business impact: production features degraded for Horizon's users across multiple services during spike window.

Environment:
- Dedicated reservation: horizons-dedicated-west (reserved-gpu-pool-12)
- Node type: 4xA100-80GB per node (mtl-config-4)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.18.2 (config: continuous-batching enabled, kv-cache default)
- Region: us-west-2

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Customer runs steady inference traffic for chat and embeddings against pinned model rw-open-7b-v2.
2. Around 2026-03-12 22:30 a scheduled long-running training transfer job (internal research tenant) started on a GPU node in the same reserved pool.
3. Within ~3-4 minutes, p95 latency for streaming and non-streaming calls rose from ~180ms to 700-1100ms; increased queueing and occasional 504s.
4. Autoscaler attempted to scale but new nodes were not provisioned quickly due to fragmentation and node packing constraints; some requests hit fallback routing to a different model variant.

Observed behavior:
- Kernel-level logs show elevated PCIe transfer retry errors and higher PCIe bus utilization on impacted nodes.
- GPU utilization reported as moderate (60-80%) but system-level PCIe stalls correlate with latency spikes.
- KV cache eviction count spiked for the affected pod group leading to repeated context restores and extra GPU memory traffic.

Expected behavior:
- Isolation of inference workloads from co-located training jobs in dedicated reservations; autoscaler to add capacity within configured cooldown and packing rules, preventing sustained p95 spikes.

Recent changes:
- Internal research scheduled a large mixed-precision training job earlier today (INT-4421).
- Autoscaler config changed 2026-03-10 to allow denser packing to increase utilization (policy: aggressive-packing-v2).

Relevant logs/metrics (links):
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/horizon/reserved-pool-12/overview
- Node-level events: https://logs.redwood.ai/stream?query=node:reserved-12+AND+pcie
- Incident trace: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/8f3b2c

Initial hypothesis:
- Noisy training job is saturating PCIe interconnect (large model weight streaming / checkpointing) causing increased device latency and repeated kernel restarts, which looks like noisy-neighbor I/O contention rather than pure compute saturation.
- Aggressive packing policy allowed training job to land on same physical host as inference pods; autoscaler sizing rules and cooldown prevented fast remediation.

Customer-facing notes (to be used in updates):
- We are investigating an I/O contention pattern on nodes in your reserved pool that coincides with a large scheduled training job. We have temporary mitigations available and are prioritizing a durable fix to prevent recurrence.
comments: Support (2026-03-13 09:12) - Asha Patel: Acknowledged. Opening investigation with infra/SRE and pinging node owners. We have asked HorizonsAI to provide recent request IDs and example traces.
Customer (2026-03-13 09:35) - Maria Gonzalez (HorizonsAI): Provided request IDs 3f9a3.. and 4b2d1.. and confirms traffic pattern is steady-state, no spikes on their side.

SRE (2026-03-13 10:05) - Diego Morales: Observed PCIe retransmit errors on nodes n-12-3 and n-12-7 coincident with training job start. Raising INT ticket for the internal training job owner and recommending immediate eviction of training pod from reserved nodes.
Infra (2026-03-13 10:40) - Priya Sharma: Initiated live migrate of training job off reserved pool nodes; evicted the training pod at 10:38. Customer p95 improved ~20 minutes after eviction.
Support (2026-03-13 11:05) - Asha Patel: Notified customer of eviction and asked to validate resumed performance; offered to apply temporary node anti-affinity to prevent co-location.

Customer (2026-03-13 11:20) - Maria Gonzalez: Confirmed tail latency improved but still seeing intermittent 504s; requested permanent solution and explanation for why autoscaler didn't add capacity faster.

SRE (2026-03-13 12:00) - Diego Morales: Found autoscaler pack policy 'aggressive-packing-v2' allowed placement that prioritized utilization over isolation. Proposing change to 'isolation-first' for dedicated pools with high-SLA customers.
Product (2026-03-13 15:45) - Lin Wei: Logged feature request to add PCIe/I/O metrics into placement scoring; will scope in next sprint.
Support (2026-03-14 08:30) - Asha Patel: Preparing next-customer update with proposed mitigations and timeline for permanent fixes.
investigation_notes: 10:05: Confirmed increased PCIe retry counters on 2/6 nodes in pool. Kernel logs show ERR entries matching driver's PCIe retry signature.
10:18: Training pod observed performing repeated large checkpoint uploads; heavy DMA traffic coincident with PCIe errors.
10:35: KV cache eviction rate for inference pods increased x8 on impacted nodes; memory pressure causing extra device<->host transfers.
10:50: Autoscaler attempted to add 2 nodes but scheduler placement failure due to packing constraints and insufficient available capacity in zone (spot provisioning lag ~7-9m).
11:30: Eviction of training pod reduced PCIe errors and lowered p95 progressively; root cause likely combined: I/O-heavy training job + packing policy + slow node provisioning.
12:15: Cross-checked with internal training owner (INT-4421): job was mis-labelled as low-priority research batch and scheduled without node-affinity limits.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-13 10:38): Evicted noisy training pod from reserved pool nodes; applied temporary node anti-affinity rule for horizon-dedicated-west reservation to prevent co-location.
Autoscaler config roll-back (2026-03-13 13:00): Reverted 'aggressive-packing-v2' to 'balanced-packing-v1' for dedicated pools with SLA in us-west-2 to prioritize isolation over density.
Short-term: Added placement rule that blocks user-initiated training jobs from scheduling onto reserved inference nodes without explicit approval. Notified research teams.
Monitoring: Added PCIe retransmit and DMA throughput to pool-level alerting and dashboards for early detection (alert: pcie_retries > 50/min on any node).
Long-term: Product/infra to implement PCIe-aware placement scoring and add autoscaler override to break packing when critical p95 thresholds triggered. Feature scoped by 2026-04 sprint.
Customer communication: Notified HorizonsAI of actions and invited to a post-incident review. Offered 1 week of elevated support and credit for impacted window.
follow_up_tasks: INT-4421: Coordinate with internal research team to add job priority metadata and node-affinity rules.
Create PR to include PCIe counters in node exporter and expose in grafana - assigned to infra team.
Update autoscaler runbook to handle PCIe/io saturation events and provide emergency isolation playbook.
Schedule postmortem and share with HorizonsAI by 2026-03-18.
